47554-gypsies-of-the-air.title: Gypsies of the Air
47554-gypsies-of-the-air.creator: Bess Moyer
47554-gypsies-of-the-air.description: A book by Bess Moyer. She was never so happy as when she was zooming to a lofty height. Her brown eyes were glowing, her ivory skin was flushed to rose as she handled the controls of her little plane. Terry claimed that the higher she flew above the earth, the better she could think and plan. But today Terry’s brain was in a whirl.

arxiv-2203-01564.title: Graph Representation Learning Beyond Node and Homophily
arxiv-2203-01564.creator: You Li, Bei Lin, Binli Luo, Ning Gui*
arxiv-2203-01564.description: Abstract Unsupervised graph representation learning aims to distill various graph information into a downstream task-agnostic dense vector embedding. However, existing graph representation learning approaches are designed mainly under the node homophily assumption: connected nodes tend to have similar labels and optimize performance on node-centric downstream tasks.

arxiv-2203-05429.title: Customized anti-reflection structure for perfect transmission through complex media
arxiv-2203-05429.creator: Michael Horodynski, Matthias Kühmayer, Clément Ferise, Stefan Rotter, Matthieu Davy
arxiv-2203-05429.description: Abstract Getting to grips with the detrimental influence of disordered environments on wave propagation is an interdisciplinary endeavour spanning diverse research areas ranging from telecommunications [ 1 ] and bio-medical imaging [ 2 ] to seismology [ 3 ] and material engineering [ 4 , 5 ] .

arxiv-2208-07910.title: When, Where, and How to Open Data
arxiv-2208-07910.creator: A Personal Perspective
arxiv-2208-07910.description: Abstract August 8, 2026 Benjamin Nachman Physics Division, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA 94720, USA Berkeley Institute for Data Science, University of California, Berkeley, CA 94720, USA ABSTRACT This is a personal perspective on data sharing in the context of public data releases suitable for generic analysis.

arxiv-2210-10553.title: Qubit-environment entanglement outside of pure decoherence: hyperfine interaction
arxiv-2210-10553.creator: Tymoteusz Salamon, Marcin Płodzień, Maciej Lewenstein, Katarzyna Roszak
arxiv-2210-10553.description: Abstract In spin-based architectures of quantum devices, the hyperfine interaction between the electron spin qubit and the nuclear spin environment remains one of the main sources of decoherence. This paper provides a short review of the current advances in the theoretical description of the qubit decoherence dynamics. Next, we study the qubit-environment entanglement using negativity as its measure.

arxiv-2307-15700.title: MeMOTR: Long-Term Memory-Augmented Transformer for Multi-Object Tracking
arxiv-2307-15700.creator: Ruopeng Gao, Limin Wang
arxiv-2307-15700.description: Abstract As a video task, Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) is expected to capture temporal information of targets effectively. Unfortunately, most existing methods only explicitly exploit the object features between adjacent frames, while lacking the capacity to model long-term temporal information. In this paper, we propose MeMOTR, a long-term memory-augmented Transformer for multi-object tracking.

arxiv-2404-07893.title: Revisiting a drag partition model for canopy-like roughness elements
arxiv-2404-07893.creator: Elia Buono, Gabriel G. Katul, Davide Vettori, Davide Poggi, Costantino Manes
arxiv-2404-07893.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Elia Buono, Gabriel G. Katul, Davide Vettori, Davide Poggi, Costantino Manes. Turbulent flows over a large surface area ( S S ) covered by n n obstacles experience an overall drag due to the presence of the ground and the protruding obstacles into the flow. The drag partition between the roughness obstacles and the ground is analyzed using an analytical model proposed by Raupach (1992) and is hereafter referred to as R92.

arxiv-2406-04007.title: Modeling the spatial resolution of magnetic solitons in Magnetic Force Microscopy and the effect on their sizes
arxiv-2406-04007.creator: I. Castro, A. Riveros, J. L. Palma, L. Abelmann, R. Tomasello, D. R. Rodrigues, A. Giordano, G. Finocchio, R. Gallardo, N. Vidal-Silva
arxiv-2406-04007.description: Abstract In this work, we explored theoretically the spatial resolution of magnetic solitons and the variations of their sizes when subjected to a Magnetic Force Microscopy (MFM) measurement. Next to tip-sample separation, we considered reversal in the magnetization direction of the tip, showing that the magnetic soliton size measurement can be strongly affected by the magnetization direction of the tip.

arxiv-2509-03527.title: Multilevel Analysis of Cryptocurrency News using RAG Approach with Fine-Tuned Mistral Large Language Model
arxiv-2509-03527.creator: Bohdan M. Pavlyshenko Ivan Franko National University of Lviv, Ukraine b.pavlyshenko@gmail.com, www.linkedin.com/in/bpavlyshenko/
arxiv-2509-03527.description: Abstract In the paper, we consider multilevel multitask analysis of cryptocurrency news using a fine-tuned Mistral 7B large language model with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). On the first level of analytics, the fine-tuned model generates graph and text summaries with sentiment scores as well as JSON representations of summaries.

pmc-10648599.title: The Role of Gut Microbiota in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus Affecting Intergenerational Glucose Metabolism: Possible Mechanisms and Interventions
pmc-10648599.creator: Yaolin Ren, Yuan Zeng, Yifan Wu, Jie Yu, Qian Zhang, Xinhua Xiao, Zohar Nachum, Enav Yefet
pmc-10648599.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The incidence of type 2 diabetes is increasing every year and has become a serious public health problem. In addition to genetic factors, environmental factors in early life development are risk factors for diabetes. There is growing evidence that the gut microbiota plays an important role in glucose metabolism, and the gut microbiota of pregnant women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) differs significantly from that of healthy pregnant women. This article reviews the role of maternal gut microbiota in offspring glucose metabolism.

pmc-10717174.title: Successful autologous stem cell transplantation for light chain proximal tubulopathy with severe kidney injury
pmc-10717174.creator: Asuka Kono, Kana Bando, Atsushi Takahata, Shigeo Toyota
pmc-10717174.description: Key Clinical MessageLight chain proximal tubulopathy (LCPT) is a rare type of monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance. Clinicians should consider LCPT in the differential diagnosis of patients with renal or proximal tubular dysfunction with monoclonal gammopathy. They should confirm diagnosis by renal biopsy and initiate chemotherapy before disease progression.

pmc-11393643.title: Correlation of RND efflux pump expression and AdeRS mutations in tigecycline-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii from Thai clinical isolates
pmc-11393643.creator: Siriphan Boonsilp, Anchalee Homkaew, Thanwa Wongsuk, Konrawee Thananon, Worrapoj Oonanant
pmc-11393643.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Tigecycline-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (TRAB) is increasing in Thailand, complicating antibiotic treatment due to limited antibiotic options. The specific resistance mechanism behind tigecycline resistance is still unclear, necessitating further investigation. We investigated the presence of OXA-type carbapenemases, the antimicrobial susceptibility profile, the inhibitory effect of carbonyl cyanide m-chlorophenylhydrazone (CCCP) on tigecycline susceptibility, the expression levels of RND-type efflux pumps and amino acid substitutions within a two-component regulatory system on 30 Thai clinical isolates.

pmc-11579344.title: Characterizing the interactions between influenza and respiratory syncytial viruses and their implications for epidemic control
pmc-11579344.creator: Sarah C. Kramer, Sarah Pirikahu, Jean-Sébastien Casalegno, Matthieu Domenech de Cellès
pmc-11579344.description: Pathogen-pathogen interactions represent a critical but little-understood feature of infectious disease dynamics. In particular, experimental evidence suggests that influenza virus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) compete with each other, such that infection with one confers temporary protection against the other. However, such interactions are challenging to study using common epidemiologic methods.

pmc-12564943.title: Protective Effects of Momordica charantia Fruit Extract on Male Sexual Dysfunction and Testicular Damage in Rats Induced by Chronic Unpredictable Stressors
pmc-12564943.creator: Therachon Kamollerd, Suwit Uopasai, Tarinee Sawatpanich, Nongnut Uabundit, Supatcharee Arun, Nareelak Tangsrisakda, Chayakorn Taoto, Chadaporn Chaimontri, Natthapol Lapyuneyong, Wipawee Thukhammee, Sararat Innoi, Sitthichai Iamsaard, Ju-Seop Kang
pmc-12564943.description: Chronic stress (CS) is known to induce testicular oxidative stress and apoptosis. Fruit of Momordica charantia (FMC) has antioxidant capacity to protect tissue damage, but its effect on sexual activity and testicular damage caused by CS has never been documented.

pmc-12581551.title: Determinants of non-adherence to iron folic acid supplementation among pregnant women attending public health facilities in Bishoftu Town, Ethiopia: case–control study
pmc-12581551.creator: Ararso Hordofa Guye, Lominat Abera, Tadesse Nigussie, Derara Girma, Berhanu Senbeta Diriba, Hiwot Dejene, Elsabeth Legesse, Daba Iticha, Leta Adugna
pmc-12581551.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIron folic acid supplementation is one of the most global public health interventions to alleviate iron deficiency anemia during pregnancy. Both folic acid and iron deficiencies constitute the major micronutrient deficiencies in Ethiopian women.

pmc-12589120.title: Outcomes of patients treated with venetoclax plus azacitidine versus azacitidine alone stratified by advanced age and acute myeloid leukemia composite model
pmc-12589120.creator: Adriano Venditti, Jing-Zhou Hou, Pierre Fenaux, Brian A Jonas, Radovan Vrhovac, Pau Montesinos, Jacqueline S Garcia, David Rizzieri, Michael J Thirman, Meng Zhang, Jalaja Potluri, Catherine Miller, Mazaher Dhalla, Vinod Pullarkat
pmc-12589120.description: Venetoclax plus azacitidine is recognized as standard of care for patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) ineligible for intensive chemotherapy (IC). However, some patients may still not be treated with venetoclax combinations due to frailty concerns. We evaluated efficacy and safety of venetoclax plus azacitidine vs.

pmc-12704305.title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with mindfulness for pain and disability management in migraine patients: a protocol feasibility study☆
pmc-12704305.creator: Fernanda Moura Vargas Dias, Renata Goltara Liboni Vescovi, Carolina Fiorin Anhoque, Maria Eduarda Pinheiro dos Santos, Christian Nogueira de Barros, Iaryssa Iris de Souza, Walter Gomes da Silva Filho, Jocemar Ilha, Fernando Zanela da Silva Arêas
pmc-12704305.description: Migraine is the second leading cause of disability worldwide, contributing to high healthcare costs, reduced work productivity, and diminished quality of life. Non-pharmacological therapies such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and mindfulness-based practices (MBPs) have independently demonstrated effectiveness in reducing headache frequency and medication use, offering safer and more tolerable alternatives to pharmacological treatments.

pmc-13454353.title: Prevalence of hearing loss and other ear disorders among patients with hepatitis B infection: a nationwide retrospective Polish cohort study
pmc-13454353.creator: Piotr Rzymski, Agnieszka Genowska, Dorota Zarębska-Michaluk, Jerzy Jaroszewicz, Krzysztof Kanecki, Katarzyna Lewtak, Paweł Goryński, Aneta Nitsch-Osuch, Robert Flisiak
pmc-13454353.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Reports from Asian populations have suggested that chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection may predispose patients to hearing impairment, particularly sudden sensorineural hearing loss, yet evidence from Europe has been lacking. To address this gap, we conducted a nationwide, retrospective analysis of the prevalence of ear and hearing disorders among patients hospitalized with HBV infection in Poland between 2012 and 2023, using the national hospital discharge database.

pmc-13544180.title: Integrating pharmacovigilance and machine learning: bleeding signal detection and risk prediction for oral anticoagulants in cancer patients
pmc-13544180.creator: Meina Lv, Xiaochun Zheng, Hang Xie, Bijuan Lin
pmc-13544180.description: BackgroundOral anticoagulants (OACs) have been widely used for the prevention and treatment of thrombosis in cancer patients, but the bleeding signals associated with different OACs in this population have not been fully studied.ObjectivesThis study aimed to compare bleeding signals, identify risk factors, and establish a prediction model for OACs in cancer patients.
